title: Nivolumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin before surgery
purpose: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

agents.name: Nivolumab
agents.explanation: Nivolumab binds PD-1 on T cells. It prevents signals that can reduce the immune attack on cancer. This can also let immune cells inflame healthy tissues. It is infused every 21 days in this plan.
agents.watch: New breathing, bowel, skin, hormone or other symptoms need prompt advice during or after treatment.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Rare serious lung or kidney injury

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Hearing changes or tinnitus, which can persist
Numbness or tingling, which can persist
Electrolyte changes and need for hydration

phases.label: Before surgery
phases.detail: Up to three 21-day cycles. Day 1: nivolumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin. Day 8: gemcitabine alone after blood tests and review. Then surgical MDT reassessment. The five listed backbones are alternatives; this guide covers only your selected combination.

phases.label: Surgical reassessment
phases.detail: The surgical team reviews scans, fitness, recovery and timing. This regimen does not automatically continue nivolumab after surgery.

timeline.label: Immune symptoms can occur any day
timeline.text: Nivolumab can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Report new symptoms promptly and carry your immune alert card for at least five months after the last dose.

day_groups.title: Day 8 treatment
day_groups.body: Gemcitabine alone if blood tests and review allow.
day_groups.action: Do not assume Day 1 clearance covers Day 8.

day_groups.title: Recovery and review
day_groups.body: Effects vary; no guaranteed recovery day.

questions.q: Will I receive all five combinations?
questions.a: No. This guide is for gemcitabine and cisplatin with nivolumab. The five backbones are alternatives; your team prescribes one.
Not automatically under this NCCP regimen. It covers at most three cycles before surgery; any later treatment needs a separate plan.

questions.q: What if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and recovery. Do not assume a delay means treatment has failed or that surgery must occur on a fixed date.

chapters.title: Your treatment before surgery
chapters.intro: This treatment is given before planned surgery for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer at high risk of returning. It aims to treat the cancer before the operation and reduce the chance of recurrence. Surgery and benefit are not guaranteed.

items.title: Why these medicines?
items.text: Nivolumab helps immune cells recognise cancer; chemotherapy damages dividing cells. Your prescribed backbone is gemcitabine and cisplatin.

items.title: Evidence and uncertainty
items.text: In a randomized study, adding nivolumab to chemotherapy before surgery improved survival compared with chemotherapy alone. Your team considers the exact cancer, test results, fitness and preferences.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Discuss surgery and other suitable treatments, clinical trials and the option of not proceeding; choices depend on the multidisciplinary assessment.

chapters.title: Treatment visits
chapters.intro: Up to three 21-day cycles. Day 1: nivolumab, gemcitabine and cisplatin. Day 8: gemcitabine alone after blood tests and review. Then surgical MDT reassessment. The five listed backbones are alternatives; this guide covers only your selected combination.

items.title: Administration
items.text: Nivolumab is infused over 30 minutes before chemotherapy. Gemcitabine is infused over 30 minutes on Days 1 and 8. Cisplatin is infused over one hour, with prescribed hydration before and afterwards. Blood-result review, preparation, support medicines and observation add to the visit.

items.title: Day-by-day checks
items.text: Blood count, kidneys, liver and glucose before each cycle; thyroid tests every 3–6 weeks; cortisol if indicated. Day 8 blood count before gemcitabine. Assess symptoms before every dose.

chapters.title: Support medicines
chapters.intro: Follow the written anti-sickness plan; Day 8 gemcitabine has its own review and support instructions. Cisplatin needs hydration, electrolyte checks and monitoring of kidneys, hearing and nerves.

chapters.title: Recognise effects early

items.title: Urgent symptoms
items.text: Contact your oncology team urgently for fever, feeling suddenly unwell, new breathlessness, chest pain, persistent diarrhoea, severe weakness, confusion, reduced urine or a severe rash. Follow your local emergency instructions; do not wait for the next appointment.

items.title: During an infusion
items.text: Tell the nurse immediately about chills, rash, flushing, chest discomfort, breathing difficulty or feeling faint.

chapters.title: Everyday care
chapters.intro: Plan support around how you feel.

items.title: Eating and drinking
items.text: Ask for help with nausea, appetite, mouth pain or poor intake. Follow any individual fluid restriction or hydration plan.

items.title: Medicines and pregnancy
items.text: Tell your team about all medicines and supplements. Discuss fertility and contraception before treatment; pregnancy and breastfeeding require specific advice.

items.title: Reassessment
items.text: Scans, clinical recovery, organ function and fitness inform the operation plan. Treatment response does not remove the need for surgical review.

items.title: Persistent effects
items.text: Nivolumab can inflame healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Report new symptoms promptly and carry your immune alert card for at least five months after the last dose.

chapters.title: Your contacts and questions
chapters.intro: Contact your oncology team urgently for fever, feeling suddenly unwell, new breathlessness, chest pain, persistent diarrhoea, severe weakness, confusion, reduced urine or a severe rash. Follow your local emergency instructions; do not wait for the next appointment.

items.title: Keep your records
items.text: Bring the treatment passport, medicines list and immune alert card to appointments or emergency care.

items.title: Understanding the plan
items.text: Ask your team to confirm the selected backbone, next visit, support medicines and whom to call.
